sections.name: INTRODUCTION
sentences: Plaintiff, Dean F. Daniels, Jr., brings this action against his former employers, Curtiss- Wright Corporation and EST Group Inc. for unlawful discrimination and retaliation, in violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, 42 U.S.C. §12101, et seq. (“ADA”), the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, as amended, 43 P.S. §951, et seq. (“PHRA”).
Plaintiff further brings this action pursuant to the Family Medical Leave Act, 29 U.S.C. §2601, et seq. (“FMLA”) for unlawful discrimination, retaliation, and leave interference.
Plaintiff seeks damages, including back-pay, front-pay, compensatory, punitive, liquidated, costs and attorneys’ fees, and all other relief that this Court deems appropriate.

sections.name: PARTIES
sentences: Plaintiff, Dean F. Daniels, Jr., is an individual and a citizen of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
He resides in Harleysville, Pennsylvania.
Defendant, Curtiss-Wright Corporation, is corporation maintaining a place of business located at 2701 Township Line Road, Hatfield, PA 19440.
Defendant, EST Group, Inc. is a corporation maintaining a place of business located at 2701 Township Line Road, Hatfield, PA 19440.
At all times material hereto, Defendants collectively constituted Plaintiff’s employer under the joint and/or single employer doctrine.
Upon information and belief, Defendants shared common management, had interrelated operations, and collectively controlled Plaintiff’s job duties and responsibilities.

At all times material hereto, Defendants acted by and through their authorized agents and/or employees acting within the course and scope of their employment with Defendants and in furtherance of Defendants’ business.
At all times material hereto, Defendants employed more than fifty (50) individuals within a seventy-five (75) mile radius of where Plaintiff worked.
At all times material hereto, Defendants were an employer within the meanings of the statutes that form the basis of this matter.
At all times material hereto, Plaintiff was an employee within the meanings of the statutes that form the basis of this matter.

sections.name: JURISDICTION AND VENUE
sentences: The causes of action that form the basis of this matter arise under the ADA, FMLA, and PHRA.
The District Court has jurisdiction over Count I (ADA) and Count II (FMLA) pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1331.
The District Court has jurisdiction over Count III (PHRA) pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1367.
Venue is proper in the District Court pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1391(b).
On July 30, 2020, Plaintiff filed a Complaint with the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (“PHRC”), cross-filed with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”).
Attached hereto, incorporated herein, and marked as Exhibit “A” is a true and correct copy of the Complaint.
On March 4, 2022, the EEOC issued to Plaintiff a Notice of Right to Sue regarding his PHRC Complaint.
Attached hereto and marked as Exhibit “B” is a true and correct copy of this notice (with minor redactions for purposes of electronic filing of confidential/identifying information).
Plaintiff is filing this complaint within ninety (90) days from his receipt of this notice.
Plaintiff has fully complied with all administrative prerequisites for the commencement of this action.

sections.name: FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
sentences: Plaintiff was employed by Defendants from in or about August 2014 until on or about July 7, 2020.
Plaintiff consistently performed his job duties in a highly competent manner and received positive feedback.
Plaintiff last held the position of Supply Chain Manager.
Plaintiff reported to Alex Kotlyar, Director, Engineering and Operations.
Kotylar reported to Jim Berneski, General Manager.
In or about February 2020, Plaintiff received a positive performance review and a merit salary increase.
Plaintiff additionally received an above-target bonus.
In or about mid-February 2020, Defendants expanded Plaintiff’s job duties, his responsibilities, and the number of his direct reports.
On or about April 8, 2020, Plaintiff was diagnosed with Major Depression Disorder, in addition to his prior Generalized Anxiety Disorder diagnosis.
These medical conditions are disabilities under the ADA and PHRA in that they substantially impair one (1) or more of Plaintiff’s major life activities.
On or about April 14, 2020, Plaintiff commenced a medically necessary leave of absence pursuant to the FMLA due to his disabilities.
Defendants had knowledge of the same.
Plaintiff’s FMLA leave was a reasonable accommodation for his disabilities.

On or about May 8, 2020, while Plaintiff was out on FMLA leave, Danielle Dixon, Berneski’s Administrative Assistant, informed Plaintiff that Berneski still wanted Plaintiff to send his updated monthly report within two (2) hours and Berneski did not care why Plaintiff was out of the office.
Plaintiff responded that he was on FMLA leave.
She apologized for the phone call and stated that she would speak with Berneski.

In or about early July 2020, Sabina Shewell, Purchasing Supervisor, commented to Plaintiff regarding his medically necessary FMLA leave that not everyone was lucky enough to have twelve (12) weeks off to catch up on their chores around the house.
On or about July 7, 2020, Plaintiff returned from his FMLA leave.
That same day, Defendants terminated Plaintiff’s employment, effective immediately.
During the termination meeting, Plaintiff stated that he believed his job was protected under FMLA.
Defendants responded that Plaintiff’s position had been eliminated due to efficiencies and that Plaintiff should not take it personally.
Defendants’ articulated reason for Plaintiff’s termination is a pretext.
Plaintiff was the only employee reporting to Kotlyar who was terminated on July 7, 2020.
Defendants assigned Plaintiff’s job duties to Shewell, who was previously Plaintiff’s direct report.
To Plaintiff’s knowledge, Shewell was not disabled, had not taken medical leave, and had not requested a reasonable accommodation for a medical condition.
Plaintiff was more qualified and experienced than Shewell.
Plaintiff’s actual and/or perceived disabilities and/or record of impairment were a motivating and/or determinative factor in Defendants’ decision to terminate Plaintiff’s employment.
Plaintiff’s request for a reasonable accommodation for his disabilities was a motivating and/or determinative factor in Defendants’ decision to terminate his employment.
By terminating Plaintiff’s employment after he returned from FMLA leave, Defendants interfered with Plaintiff’s right to protected leave under the FMLA.
By terminating Plaintiff’s employment after he took FMLA leave, Defendants discriminated and retaliated against Plaintiff for invoking his rights under the FMLA.
Plaintiff’s invocation of his rights under the FMLA was a motivating and/or determinative factor in Defendants’ decision to terminate his employment.
Defendants’ violations of the FMLA were willful.

As a direct and proximate result of the discriminatory and retaliatory conduct of Defendants, Plaintiff has in the past incurred and may in the future incur a loss of earnings and/or earning capacity, loss of benefits, pain and suffering, embarrassment, humiliation, loss of self- esteem, mental anguish, and loss of life’s pleasures.

Plaintiff is now suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable injury and monetary damages as a result of Defendants’ discriminatory and retaliatory acts unless and until this Court grants the relief requested herein.

sections.name: COUNT I – ADA
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates herein by reference the paragraphs above, as if set forth herein in their entirety.

By committing the foregoing acts of discrimination and retaliation against Plaintiff, Defendants violated the ADA. Defendants acted with malice or a reckless indifference to Plaintiff’s rights, thereby warranting the imposition of punitive damages.
As a direct and proximate result of Defendants’ violation of the ADA, Plaintiff has suffered the injuries, damages, and losses set forth herein.
Plaintiff has incurred and is entitled to reasonable costs and attorneys’ fees incurred as a result of the unlawful behavior complained of herein.
No previous application has been made for the relief requested herein.

sections.name: COUNT II – FMLA
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates by reference the paragraphs above, as if set forth herein in their entirety.
By committing the foregoing acts against Plaintiff, Defendants violated the FMLA.
By terminating Plaintiff after he used protected leave and/or requested protected leave, Defendants discriminated and retaliated against Plaintiff and violated the FMLA.
By terminating Plaintiff’s employment upon his return from FMLA leave, Defendants interfered with Plaintiff’s ability to use protected leave under the FMLA.
Said violations were willful.
The imposition of liquidated damages is warranted.
As a direct and proximate result of Defendants’ violations of the FMLA, Plaintiff has suffered the damages and losses set forth herein.
Plaintiff has incurred and is entitled to reasonable costs and attorneys’ fees incurred as a result of the unlawful behavior complained of herein.
No previous application has been made for the relief requested herein.

sections.name: COUNT III – PHRA
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates by reference the paragraphs above, as if set forth herein in their entirety.
By discriminating and retaliating against Plaintiff, Defendants violated the PHRA.
As a direct and proximate result of Defendants’ violation of the PHRA, Plaintiff has sustained the injuries, damages, and losses set forth herein.
Plaintiff has incurred and is entitled to reasonable costs and attorneys’ fees incurred as a result of the unlawful behavior complained of herein.
No previous application has been made for the relief requested herein.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff seeks damages and legal and equitable relief in connection with Defendants’ improper conduct, and specifically prays that the Court grant the following relief to Plaintiff by: a. declaring the acts and practices complained of herein to be in violation of the ADA; b. declaring the acts and practices complained of herein to be in violation of the FMLA; c. declaring the acts and practices complained of herein to be in violation of the PHRA; d. enjoining and restraining permanently the violations alleged herein; e. awarding Plaintiff back-pay; f. awarding Plaintiff front-pay; g. awarding interest; h. awarding compensatory damages to Plaintiff for past and future pain and suffering, emotional upset, mental anguish, humiliation, and loss of life’s pleasures, which Plaintiff has suffered or may suffer as a result of Defendants’ improper conduct; i. awarding liquidated damages; j. awarding punitive damages; k. awarding Plaintiff the costs of this action, together with reasonable attorneys’ fees; l. awarding Plaintiff such other damages as are appropriate under the ADA, FMLA, and PHRA; and m. granting such other and further relief as this Court deems appropriate.
